title: Prof. Dr.
name: Ali Maximilian Ertürk
bio: Director of iBIO. Enabling technologies for personalized treatment of complex diseases.
biography:
I obtained my undergraduate degree from Bilkent University in Ankara in 2003, and my Ph.D. at LMU Munich while working at the Max Planck Institute of Neurobiology, focusing on axon regeneration in the injured spinal cord. In 2009, I moved to Genentech in South San Francisco as a postdoc, where I worked on non-apoptotic caspase-3 actions in neurodegeneration, traumatic brain injury, and whole-brain tissue clearing to assess neurodegeneration.

Currently, I am Director of the Institute for Intelligent Biotechnologies (iBIO) at Helmholtz Munich and Professor at LMU Munich. I am very excited about developing and implementing technologies to enable personalized treatment of complicated diseases — from wildDISCO and DeepMACT to DISCO-MS, MouseMapper, and SCP-Nano. Besides chasing breakthrough science with my team, I enjoy sports, photography, reading, and cooking.
researchInterests: Whole-body tissue clearing, light-sheet microscopy, AI-based organ mapping, spatial omics, and nanotechnology for precision medicine and neurodegeneration.

career.description: Director, Institute for Intelligent Biotechnologies (iBIO), Helmholtz Munich; Professor, LMU Munich
Postdoctoral fellow, Genentech, South San Francisco — neurodegeneration and whole-brain tissue clearing
PhD research, LMU Munich / Max Planck Institute of Neurobiology — axon regeneration after spinal cord injury

title: Dr.
name: Markus Elsner
bio: Deputy Director of iBIO; former Nature Biotechnology editor.
biography:
I studied biochemistry at the University of Frankfurt (Germany) and the University of Bath (UK) as an undergraduate. For my graduate work, I moved to EMBL in Heidelberg and the University of Gothenburg (Sweden), where I characterized protein dynamics in living cells.

As a postdoc at the National Institutes of Health in Bethesda (USA), I investigated the mechanisms of lipid and protein sorting during membrane transport events in mammalian cells. In 2008, I became an editor at Nature Biotechnology, focusing on genome engineering, imaging, and cancer therapy papers. Since 2022, I am Deputy Director of iBIO.

Outside work, I am a bit of a history buff and enjoy cycling and traveling.
researchInterests: Genome engineering, imaging technologies, cancer therapy, and scientific publishing at the interface of biotechnology innovation.

career.description: Deputy Director, iBIO, Helmholtz Munich
Editor, Nature Biotechnology
National Institutes of Health, Bethesda — lipid and protein sorting during membrane transport

title: Dr.
name: Farida Hellal
bio: Pioneer in tissue clearing and light-sheet microscopy.
biography:
I studied Biochemistry in Paris at Pierre & Marie Curie University, where I received a master's degree in Neurosciences. I completed an industrial Ph.D. in Pharmacology on drug development for traumatic brain injury.

As a postdoc, I joined the Max Planck Institute of Neurobiology Munich and DZNE in Bonn, where I uncovered the relevance of manipulating the cytoskeleton to promote axonal regeneration after spinal cord injury and contributed with Ali Ertürk to the development of tissue clearing and imaging by light-sheet microscopy. I moved to the Institute for Stroke and Dementia Research to investigate neuronal network remodeling after stroke.

I am fond of not only science but also social anthropology, philosophizing on the meaning of life over a glass of wine, and French cooking and baking for others.
researchInterests: Axonal regeneration, tissue clearing, light-sheet microscopy, stroke, and neuronal network remodeling.

name: Thomas Schubert
bio: Translates innovative biotechnologies into real-world applications at iBIO.
biography:
I obtained my PhD in Biochemistry from the University of Regensburg, where I studied how snoRNAs influence chromatin accessibility and developed a strong interest in biophysics. Alongside a short postdoc, I completed a business degree (Betriebswirt IWW), which helped bridge my scientific and entrepreneurial interests.

I was part of the founding team of 2bind GmbH, where I served as CEO for 12 years, driving the company's growth at the interface of biophysics and drug discovery. I have now joined iBIO as Head of Operations in Biotechnology, focusing on translating innovative technologies into real-world applications.

Outside of work, I enjoy escape rooms, cooking, spending time with friends, and challenging myself on the rowing machine.
title: Dr.
Dr.
name: Harsharan S. Bhatia
bio: Spatial omics and DISCO-MS; neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration.
biography:
I received my Bachelor's in Biology from Punjabi University, India and my Master's in Biotechnology from Dehradun University. Afterwards I moved to Freiburg, Germany to undertake a PhD at Albert-Ludwigs University, studying the role of antioxidants in regulating microglia-driven inflammation in vitro.

Since completing my PhD I've worked as a postdoc at UCLA, California, studying how dietary manipulations during gestation affect synaptic plasticity and behaviour, then back to Freiburg as a Research Associate examining how epigenetic factors regulate microglial function in chronic neuroinflammation. I joined the Ertürk Lab in 2017 to elucidate underlying molecular mechanisms in chronic neuroinflammation associated neurodegeneration and now lead omics technologies including DISCO-MS spatial proteomics and DISCO-seq.

I love cricket, cooking Indian cuisine, and Bollywood songs.
researchInterests: Spatial proteomics (DISCO-MS), DISCO-seq, chronic neuroinflammation, and neurodegeneration.

title: Dr.
name: Ceren Kimna
bio: Targeted drug delivery and lipid nanoparticle formulations.
biography:
I was born in Izmir and pursued a Bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering at Ege University. Later, I earned a Master's degree in Chemical Engineering from the Izmir Institute of Technology where I additionally worked as a research assistant for two years. I also hold a Bachelor's degree in Business Administration and a Master's degree in Pharmacognosy.

In summer 2018, I moved to Munich to begin my PhD studies at the Technical University of Munich, focusing on the development of targeted drug delivery systems. My expertise led me to join the Ertürk Lab in February 2023, where I develop novel lipid nanoparticle formulations and targeted delivery strategies.

In my free time, I enjoy cooking, traveling, diving, and spending time with my two cats, Bulut and Midas.
researchInterests: Lipid nanoparticles, targeted drug delivery, and nanotechnology for therapeutic applications.

title: Dr.
name: Philip Ruthig
bio: Neuroscientist, data scientist, and microscopist.
biography:
My name is Philip, and I studied Neuroscience and Molecular Biology in the beautiful city of Heidelberg, where I became fascinated with brain function and structure. Therefore, I moved to Leipzig University for my PhD and PostDoc to work on auditory lateralization and human white matter structure. During that time, I was introduced to DISCO clearing, light sheet microscopy, and learned how to handle and analyze huge datasets efficiently – which is also what I do as a staff scientist here.

Other than science, I have a passion for music concerts and love to do outdoor sports like rope climbing and kitesurfing.
researchInterests: DISCO tissue clearing, light-sheet microscopy, white matter structure, and terabyte-scale imaging data analysis.

title: Dr.
name: Doris Kaltenecker
bio: Molecular biologist studying systemic metabolic diseases.
biography:
I studied molecular biotechnology in Vienna and completed my Ph.D. at the Medical University of Vienna, investigating how JAK-STAT signaling regulates adipose tissue and liver metabolism.

My work focuses on cancer-associated weight loss and obesity, tissue clearing, light-sheet microscopy, and AI-based image analysis to study disease across organs and the whole body.

Outside the lab, I enjoy traveling, exploring nature, practicing pilates and chasing sunsets wherever I go.
researchInterests: Whole-body imaging, deep learning for organ mapping, MouseMapper, and metabolic biology.

title: Dr.
name: Jennifer Modamio
bio: Cancer organoid screening for metastasis and treatment resistance.
biography:
Originally from Spain, I obtained a B.Sc. in Molecular Biology from the University of Salamanca and completed an internship at the IMIB (Würzburg, Germany). I got an M.Sc. in Biomedicine applied to cancer research from the University of Barcelona, analyzing lncRNAs in follicular lymphoma progression.

I obtained my Ph.D. in Systems Biomedicine from the University of Luxembourg, exploring alpha-synuclein toxicity in patient-derived midbrain organoids for Parkinson's disease. I joined the Ertürk Lab in 2022 as a postdoc to set up a screening pipeline for cancer organoids to investigate treatment resistance and metastasis and develop new cancer therapies.

In my spare time, I enjoy long hikes in sunny weather, live music, reading, and cooking.
researchInterests: Cancer organoids, treatment resistance, metastasis, and high-throughput screening pipelines.

title: Dr.
name: Mihail Todorov
bio: Brain vasculature in health and disease; VesSAP.
biography:
I was born in Bulgaria and grew up in Hungary. After obtaining my Master's degree as a Biologist (specialisation in Neuroscience and Human Biology) from Eötvös Loránd University, I did my PhD at the Graduate School of Systemic Neurosciences.

My former research focus was in vivo rodent visual and in vitro electrophysiology, single-cell PCR, patch-clamp, and batch data analysis. Now I'm focused on the vascular network of the brain during health and disease, building on the VesSAP platform.

My interests include travelling, electronics, and hiking.
researchInterests: Brain vasculature, VesSAP, electrophysiology, and vascular networks in health and disease.

title: Dr.
name: Louis Kümmerle
bio: Machine learning on single-cell and spatial transcriptomics.
biography:
I grew up in a small village close to Heilbronn, Germany. I obtained a B.Sc. in Biochemistry and a B.Sc. in Physics from the University of Würzburg, then moved to Tübingen for an M.Sc. in Neural Information Processing at the Graduate Training Center for Neuroscience.

In January 2020 I started my Ph.D. in the Ertürk Lab and Theis Lab. My work focuses on developing and applying machine learning methods on single-cell transcriptomics and spatial transcriptomics.

In my spare time I like playing the guitar and doing sports like running and badminton.
researchInterests: Machine learning, single-cell transcriptomics, and spatial transcriptomics.

name: Ying Chen
bio: Deep learning for biomedical data processing and analysis.
biography:
I was born and raised in Sichuan Province of China. I obtained my Bachelor's and Master's degrees from Beihang University on pattern recognition and intelligent systems, focusing on deep learning methods for cerebral arterial segmentation in magnetic resonance angiography volumes.

In October 2022, I started my PhD studies at LMU and joined the Ertürk Lab. My main interest is introducing deep learning methods into biomedical data processing and analysis.

In my spare time, I like to play badminton, swim, and cook.
researchInterests: Deep learning, biomedical image analysis, and pattern recognition.

name: Jie Zhang
bio: Accelerating tissue clearing for large specimens.
biography:
I'm from Xinjiang, China. I studied bioengineering at Hubei University of Technology, then completed my master's in biological and pharmaceutical engineering at Northwestern Polytechnical University, focusing on polymer-based delivery systems for efficient RNA delivery.

In April 2024, I started my PhD studies at LMU and joined the Ertürk Lab. My work explores different conditions to accelerate the process of tissue clearing.

In my free time, I like hiking, swimming, and traveling.
researchInterests: Tissue clearing optimization, polymer delivery systems, and large-specimen imaging.

name: Eva Küsters
bio: Ph.D. candidate studying cancer across the whole mouse body with tissue clearing and spatial omics.
biography:
I studied biology for my bachelor's degree in Göttingen before moving to Ulm for my master's, where I specialized in Molecular and Translational Neuroscience. During this time I became interested in advanced spatial sequencing techniques and how they could be used to study biology at high resolution. This interest in spatial methods led me to join the lab, where I could dive deeper into tissue clearing.

As a PhD Candidate in the lab, my work now centers on studying cancer across the whole mouse body using tissue clearing, with the aim of uncovering interactions that are easily missed with conventional, 2D approaches. A particular focus of mine is understanding how peripheral nerves communicate with cancer cells — a question that benefits directly from being able to look at intact tissue in three dimensions.

Alongside imaging, I'm working to bring new omics techniques into the lab's workflow, so that what we observe in 3D can be analyzed in greater molecular depth. This sits at the intersection of tissue clearing, spatial omics, and pathology — and I enjoy the collaborative, interdisciplinary nature of the work, drawing on expertise from across the lab and beyond.

Outside of work, I like spending time outdoors — hiking and biking — as well as time with my partner and our dog.
researchInterests: Whole-body tissue clearing, neuroscience, spatial omics, proteomics, cancer models, and pathological stainings.

name: Qi Liu
bio: Foundation models and machine learning for biomedical data.
biography:
I am Qi Liu (刘奇), born and raised in Hubei Province, China. In 2018, I received my Bachelor's in Electronic Information Science and Technology from China University of Mining and Technology. In 2021, I obtained my Master's in Control Engineering from Tsinghua University, focusing on machine learning and bioinformatics.

After three years in industry at the Global Health Drug Discovery Institute in Beijing, I started my Ph.D. at LMU in December 2024 and joined the Ertürk Lab. My work is on machine learning, foundation models, and biomedical data analysis.

In my spare time, I enjoy playing badminton, cooking, and photography.
researchInterests: Foundation models, machine learning, bioinformatics, and biomedical imaging data analysis.

title: Dr.
name: Laurent Simons
bio: Physics and medicine at the interface of whole-body biology.
biography:
Hi, I am Laurent Simons from Belgium. After obtaining my Bachelor's and Master's degrees in Physics, I started my PhD in (Quantum) Physics which I am about to complete. I recently joined the Ertürk Lab because of its cutting-edge research and tendency to explore uncharted territory in science, for a second PhD in Medicine.

Besides my passion for science and tech, I very much like hanging out with friends and movie (especially Marvel) marathons.
researchInterests: Quantum physics, whole-body imaging technologies, and interdisciplinary approaches bridging physics and medicine.

name: Luciano Höher
bio: Biologist specialized in 3D/VR data visualization and analysis.
biography:
I studied biology for my bachelor at LMU Munich and joined as a student assistant. I'm self-taught in virtual reality visualization and analysis during my time at the Ertürk Lab. Starting my master program in life science in 2026.

My responsibilities in the lab are visualization, analysis and creation of ground truth data for our 3D data sets in virtual reality. I'm involved in most imaging projects and train/supervise students for our VR work.
researchInterests: Virtual Reality, biomedical 3D imaging data visualization and analysis, neuroscience, machine learning / AI.

name: Zairong Cai
bio: Master's thesis in the Nanotech Team.
biography:
My name is Zairong (Tsai-ing, in Hokkien). I am originally from Quanzhou, a UNESCO World Cultural Heritage City. I began my academic journey in chemistry at Fuzhou University and later at the Technical University of Kaiserslautern.

I moved to Munich for my Master's at TUM, focusing on biochemistry and organic chemistry. In October 2025, I joined the Nanotech Team at the Ertürk Lab to complete my Master's thesis.

In my spare time, I enjoy exploring cities and nature, cooking, and learning languages.

name: Marin Bralo
bio: Laboratory support across clearing and imaging pipelines.
biography:
I was born in Livno, Bosnia and Herzegovina, where I attended elementary and high school. I obtained my Bachelor's and Master's degrees in Biology and Chemistry from the University of Split in Croatia. In my Master's thesis I performed biochemical studies on tyrocidine synthetase variants (nonribosomal peptide synthetases producing the antibiotic tyrocidine).

I also worked as a biology and chemistry teacher. Besides doing and teaching science I enjoy hiking, weightlifting, good music, movies, and meeting new people.

name: Denise Jeridi
bio: Biology lab technician at Helmholtz Munich.
biography:
After graduating from high school, I completed a voluntary social year in the emergency room at a hospital. During my science propaedeutic seminar, I studied sport and its influence on the brain as part of the nervous system, which led me to train as a biology lab technician at Helmholtz Munich — and ultimately to work on interesting topics with an amazing team in the Ertürk Lab.

In my free time I enjoy listening to music, going to concerts, or juggling.

name: Xiaoshan Hu

biography:
I am from Mainland China. Before settling in Munich, I worked as a civil engineer in a construction design company for more than ten years in Beijing after obtaining my Bachelor's degree. In February 2022 I joined the Ertürk Lab as team assistant and I am fascinated by the group's research in imaging and molecular analysis.

In my free time I enjoy metal music and traveling, and I am also interested in architecture and interior design.

name: Stefanie Reitinger
bio: Project coordination and communications.
biography:
Hi, my name is Stefanie. After obtaining my Bachelor's degree in Business Communications, I started working in various companies across Europe to gain professional experience while exploring new places and cultures. I joined the Ertürk Lab in January 2022 because I wanted to be part of a team that strives for a better future.

When I'm not working, I'm a writer and a huge book nerd. I also enjoy baking and working out (just so I can eat more sweets)!

name: Gözde Ünver
bio: AI Scientist at iBIO. Working on 3D virtual H&E generation from 3D light-sheet microscopy images.
biography:
I joined the Ertürk Lab in March 2026 as an AI Scientist. My work focuses on 3D virtual H&E generation from 3D light-sheet microscopy images.

I completed my M.Sc. in Informatics at TUM and my B.Sc. in Computer Engineering at Boğaziçi University.
researchInterests: 3D virtual H&E generation from light-sheet microscopy images, machine learning, and biomedical imaging.

name: Ahmet Sarigun
bio: AI Scientist working on Agentic AI for science at iBIO, Munich, Germany.
biography:
I am an AI Scientist at Helmholtz Munich, Institute for Intelligent Biotechnologies (iBIO), Munich, Germany. I joined the Ertürk Lab in May 2026, where my work focuses on Agentic AI for science — building systems that can plan, reason, and act across scientific workflows.

Before Munich, I worked as a Scientist at the Max Delbrück Center (MDC-BIMSB) in Berlin, Germany on structure-based drug design and bioinformatics. I studied Chemistry at METU in Ankara, Turkey, with research in graph representation learning, deep learning for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, and de novo drug design.

Outside work, I enjoy running and cycling, and occasionally make educational animations in quantum chemistry with Manim.
researchInterests: Agentic AI for science, machine learning for biology and chemistry, structure-based drug design, graph neural networks, and multi-omics data integration.

bio: Molecular biologist interested in neuroimmunology.

I joined the Ertürk Lab in August 2026 as a Ph.D. Candidate in the Graduate School of Systemic Neurosciences.

I studied Molecular Biology, Genetics and Bioengineering at Sabancı University, then completed an M.Sc. in Molecular and Cellular Biology at LMU Munich. During my master's thesis I worked as a Research Assistant at iBIO, Helmholtz Munich, and I completed additional research internships in Nuclear Medicine at LMU Hospital and in Large Molecule Research at Roche.

My research interests are at the intersection of neuroscience and immunology.

title: Dr.
name: Kuan-Ting Pan
bio: Mass spectrometry, proteomics, and AI.
biography:
I'm a mass spectrometry and proteomics enthusiast, moving between academic research and industry, and between fundamental method development and translating ideas into things people can actually use. At the institute, I'm responsible for proteomics operations and development.

These days I'm especially curious about how AI is moving into this space and quietly changing the whole field — from how data gets generated to what we can actually learn from it. It's great to be working at that intersection.
researchInterests: Mass spectrometry, proteomics, and AI.

title: Dr.
name: Danielle Beckman
bio: Neuroscientist interested in virology & microscopy.
biography:
I am a neuroscientist born and raised in Rio, Brazil. I completed technical training in Biotechnology, earned a bachelor's degree in Pharmacy, a master's degree in Biophysics, and a PhD in Biological Chemistry. Following my doctoral training, I moved to the United States to work at the California National Primate Center. In 2026, I joined the Ertürk Lab in Munich.

My research initially focused on applying high-resolution microscopy to better understand the neurodegenerative processes associated with Alzheimer's disease. Over time, my interests expanded to investigating the neurological consequences of viral infections, including those caused by the Zika virus, HIV, and, more recently, SARS-CoV-2. A major goal of my work is to contribute to the development of novel therapies and the identification of biomarkers for post-acute infection syndromes such as Long Covid.

Outside the laboratory, I enjoy going to movie theaters, strength training, reading science fiction, and spending time with my two cats.
researchInterests: Neuroscience, high-resolution microscopy, viral neurological consequences, Alzheimer's disease, and post-acute infection syndromes.

name: Emirhan Yagmur
bio: Ph.D. candidate developing ML frameworks for de novo peptide and protein design.
biography:
I studied Molecular Biotechnology at TUM, completing my B.Sc. and my M.Sc. with specializations in bioinformatics, machine learning, protein design, genetic engineering, and neuroscience.

I am now a Ph.D. candidate in the Ertürk Lab, where I develop machine learning frameworks for de novo peptide and protein design aimed at cell-specific delivery.

Outside work, I enjoy reading, traveling, and sports.
researchInterests: Machine learning, protein design, cell-specific delivery, and bioinformatics.

bio: Master's thesis on predicting LNP formulations; bioinformatics and machine learning.
biography:
My name is Sun. I studied Biomedicine at Fudan University in Shanghai for my bachelor's. Now I am doing my master's in Biology at LMU, shifting more toward the interdisciplinary area of bioinformatics, machine learning, and human health.

I joined the Ertürk Lab for my master's thesis, which is focused on the prediction task of different LNP formulations.
